newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SEES NATIONAL LOTTERY BY 2ND HALF 1998.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SEES NATIONAL LOTTERY BY 2ND HALF 1998.

text.p: South Africa's trade and industry department said on Friday that the country should have a national lottery in place by the second half of 1998.
The department outlined in a statement the procedure and expected timing for setting up the lottery.

The government will revise the draft Lotteries Bill to incorporate international contributions and local responses. It is expected the bill will be enacted no later than July 1997 after which the Lotteries Board would be formally constituted.

A lottery operator's licence will also be drafted to govern operations. The statement said that it was envisaged that the state would play a primary regulatory role via the Board, with commerical operations performed by the operator.
Market research on lottery matters is expected to be completed by September this year.
Tenderers for the lottery will be given about three months to submit bids resulting in responses being required by the end of November or early December.

"Detailed comparative evaluation process of bids will take approximately three months so that the successful tenderer for the contract for the national lottery will be announced in March/April 1998," the statement said.
The department said that the schedule was a relatively optimistic scenario and would be based on "timeous decision-making by the relevant authorities."
